name: Bivamelagon
lead: Bivamelagon (also LB54640) is an investigational oral drug that activates the melanocortin-4 receptor (MC4R), a brain pathway involved in appetite and energy balance. It is being developed for hypothalamic obesity, weight gain that follows damage to the hypothalamus, and its appearance relevance is through body weight and body fat: a drug that lowers hunger and weight could change body composition and how lean a person looks [1][2][3].

Wikipedia describes it as a small-molecule MC4 receptor agonist under development by LG Chem Life Sciences, and notes that unlike the older MC4R agonist setmelanotide, which is given by injection, it can be taken by mouth [4][5]. Setmelanotide (Imcivree) was approved in the US in November 2020 and in the EU in July 2021 for obesity caused by certain rare genetic conditions [5].

A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 trial in acquired hypothalamic obesity was reported in the Journal of the Endocrine Society in 2025 [1]. A registered phase 2 study (n=28) is complete and a long-term extension study (n=25) began enrolling by invitation in November 2025 [2][3]. Bivamelagon is not an approved drug.

chain: Oral MC4R agonist acts on the brain's appetite pathway
Lower hunger and body weight in people with hypothalamic obesity
Reduction in body fat and a leaner appearance (not studied in healthy people)
angle.text: Bivamelagon is being studied to reduce weight in a rare medical form of obesity. Any link to looks runs through body weight and fat, and no study has examined it for cosmetic fat loss in healthy people.

paras: Bivamelagon is a small-molecule agonist of the melanocortin-4 receptor [4]. Setmelanotide, which acts at the same receptor, activates MC4 receptors in the hypothalamus that regulate appetite, increases resting energy expenditure and, unlike some other MC4R agonists, does not raise heart rate or blood pressure according to Wikipedia [5]. Wikipedia reports that in two one-year studies of 10 and 11 participants most lost more than 10 percent of initial body weight on setmelanotide, and some reported feeling less hungry [5].

Common setmelanotide side effects listed there include injection-site reactions, skin hyperpigmentation, headache and gastrointestinal problems [5]. Wikipedia lists bivamelagon among other MC4 agonists without describing its adverse effects [4].

Wikipedia cites a 2022 first-in-human safety and pharmacodynamics study in the journal Obesity and notes that phase 2 trials were complete as of February 2026, with Rhythm Pharmaceuticals named in connection with the trials [4]. The registry listing NCT06046443 began in July 2024 and is complete, and NCT07156578 is a long-term follow-up study started in November 2025 [2][3].

The phase 2 trial in acquired hypothalamic obesity tested once-daily oral bivamelagon against placebo and was reported as a 2025 conference abstract [1]. The registry listing NCT06046443 is complete, and NCT07156578 is a long-term follow-up [2][3]. No studies were found in healthy people seeking cosmetic fat loss.

timeline.event: Setmelanotide, the injectable MC4R agonist, is approved in the US [5].
First-in-human safety and pharmacodynamics study of bivamelagon is published in Obesity [4].
Phase 2 study in hypothalamic obesity begins [2].
Phase 2 results presented; long-term study starts [1][3].

card.summary: Investigational oral MC4R agonist tested for hypothalamic obesity; no data in cosmetic use.
card.note: Not approved; studied only in a rare medical obesity.

quick.overview:
Bivamelagon is an experimental once-daily oral drug that activates the MC4R, a brain receptor involved in appetite and weight regulation.

It has been tested in a phase 2 trial in people with hypothalamic obesity. It is not approved.
quick.mechanism: It stimulates MC4R signaling in the brain's weight-regulating pathway.
quick.risks: Not approved anywhere; safety data are limited to early trials in a small patient group.
